"""
Final verification that NO_COLOR support works according to https://no-color.org/
"""

import os
from io import StringIO
from loguru import logger


def test_no_color_spec_compliance():
    """Test that we comply with NO_COLOR specification."""
    print("Testing NO_COLOR compliance...")
    
    # According to https://no-color.org/:
    # "When the NO_COLOR environment variable is present and set to any value 
    # (even an empty string), programs that usually output colored text should 
    # disable ANSI color output and fall back to uncolored output."
    
    test_values = ['', '1', 'true', 'false', '0', 'anything']
    
    for value in test_values:
        print(f"\nTesting NO_COLOR={repr(value)}:")
        
        # Set the environment variable
        os.environ['NO_COLOR'] = value
        
        try:
            # Test explicit colorize=True (this should be overridden)
            output = StringIO()
            handler_id = logger.add(output, format="<green>{message}</green>", colorize=True)
            logger.info("Test message")
            logger.remove(handler_id)
            
            result = output.getvalue()
            has_colors = '\x1b[' in result
            
            print(f"  Result: {repr(result.strip())}")
            print(f"  Has ANSI codes: {has_colors}")
            
            if has_colors:
                print(f"  ❌ FAIL: Should not have colors when NO_COLOR={repr(value)}")
                return False
            else:
                print(f"  ✅ PASS: Correctly disabled colors")
                
        finally:
            # Clean up
            del os.environ['NO_COLOR']
    
    print("\n✅ All NO_COLOR tests passed! Specification compliant.")
    return True


def test_normal_behavior_preserved():
    """Test that normal behavior is preserved when NO_COLOR is not set."""
    print("\nTesting normal behavior preservation...")
    
    # Without NO_COLOR, explicit colorize=True should work
    output = StringIO()
    handler_id = logger.add(output, format="<green>{message}</green>", colorize=True)
    logger.info("Colored message")
    logger.remove(handler_id)
    
    result = output.getvalue()
    has_colors = '\x1b[' in result
    
    print(f"Result: {repr(result.strip())}")
    print(f"Has ANSI codes: {has_colors}")
    
    if not has_colors:
        print("❌ FAIL: Should have colors when NO_COLOR is not set")
        return False
